items.new: But it may be supposed that from the naked skeleton of the stranded whale, accurate hints may be gathered about his true form. Not at all. For it is one of the more curious things about this Leviathan that his skeleton gives very little idea of his general shape. Though Jeremy Bentham's skeleton, which hangs as a candelabrum in the library of one of his executors, correctly conveys the idea of a burly-browed utilitarian old gentleman, with all of Jeremy's other leading personal characteristics, nothing of this kind could be inferred from any leviathan's articulated bones. In fact, as the great anatomist Hunter says, the mere skeleton of the whale bears the same relation to the fully clothed and padded animal as the insect does to the chrysalis that so roundly envelops it. This peculiarity is strikingly evident in the head, as will be incidentally shown in some part of this book. It is also very curiously displayed in the side fin, the bones of which correspond almost exactly to the bones of the human hand, minus only the thumb. This fin has four regular bone-fingers: the index, middle, ring, and little finger. But all these are permanently lodged in their fleshy covering, as human fingers are in an artificial covering. "However recklessly the whale may sometimes serve us," said humorous Stubb one day, "he can never truly be said to handle us without mittens."

items.new: Whatever superstitions the sperm whalemen in general have connected with the sight of this object, it is certain that the very rarity of a glimpse of it has gone far to invest it with ominous significance. So rarely is it seen that, though one and all of them declare it to be the largest living thing in the ocean, very few of them have any but the vaguest ideas about its true nature and form; nevertheless, they believe it furnishes the sperm whale with his only food. For though other species of whales find their food above water, and may be seen by man in the act of feeding, the spermaceti whale obtains his whole food in unknown zones below the surface; and only by inference can anyone tell what, precisely, that food consists of. At times, when closely pursued, he will vomit up what are supposed to be the detached arms of the squid, some of those thus brought up exceeding twenty and thirty feet in length. They imagine that the monster to which these arms belonged ordinarily clings by them to the bed of the ocean; and that the sperm whale, unlike other species, is supplied with teeth in order to attack and tear it.
